pattern_stance_changes.reason: Tables VII–VIII report cost, tokens and calls, but no budget or cap mechanism is tested. The retry cap is fixed at 3 and never varied. Reporting cost is not evidence that budgets or caps work.

Both arms are single-agent (§VII-B). The comparison is single-pass generation vs a validator-driven retry loop, not single-agent vs multi-agent or orchestrated designs. Equal quality comes from one model and one run with a confounded loop (§IX-B), so it says nothing about P10.

§IX-B says the loop received 'general structural feedback' rather than the specific checker output (node-level Axe findings), so linter or static-analysis feedback in the loop was never actually tested. The hybrid LLM-plus-rule-engine design the paper recommends is not run. No measured evidence points either way.

missed_issues: The provenance of the negatives is inconsistent. Table I labels the sets 'scraped_sites' and 'scraped_sites_fixed', and §VI-C says residual violations remain 'due to limitations in automated remediation', which suggests automatically produced fixes. §VII-A instead says the negatives are AccessGuru snippets 'corrected by authors with frontend expertise'. The detection ground truth is therefore of unclear origin.

Table X ('sample before–after rule table') uses generic filenames (site_home.html, checkout.html, dashboard.html) that do not match the dataset's naming (arstechnica_com_*, act-rules_github_io_* in Tables XI–XII), and its deltas are nearly uniform (−3 to −5). It looks illustrative rather than measured, while Table XI's real pages show mostly zero or positive deltas.
Table III gives rule-based detection rates of 45% (syntax) and 40% (layout), which is hard to reconcile with Axe-Core recall of 0.93 in Table II; the category framing is not explained.
Repair is evaluated on 308 of the 331 violating pages with no account of the missing 23.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats and with the review's claim grading and its P16 'contradicts' stance, which is properly caveated as a weak-feedback loop. Three peripheral stances (P24, P10, P17) credit evidence the paper never measures. Data provenance and an apparently illustrative Table X add to the integrity concerns.
